# '''Focus on the tried and true.''' Ultimately, losing weight comes down to one key principle: Burn more calories than you consume. The steps that follow won't work if you have a thousand more calories coming into your body on a daily basis than you have going out. Lay the foundation for weight loss with these practices:
#*Count calories and [[Keep a Food Diary|keep a food diary]].
#*[[Keep to Your Diet|Go on a diet.]]
#*Cut down on [[Eat Less Sugar|sugar]], [[Avoid High Fructose Corn Syrup|high fructose corn syrup]], [[Avoid Trans Fats|trans fats]] and [[Limit Your Saturated Fat Intake|saturated fats]].
#* Burn more calories by [[Exercise|exercising]]: [[Run]], [[Walk|walk]], even [[Exercise While Sitting at Your Computer|exercise at the computer]] you are sitting in front of now.
#* [[Increase Your Metabolism|Raise your metabolism.]]

# [[Image:Bowlmaccheese_73.jpg|thumb|Big bowl, big servings, big weight gain]]'''Downsize your kitchenware.''' The human mind works in mysterious ways. It turns out that using smaller bowls, plates, and containers can subconsciously influence how much you serve yourself. Even nutrition experts are victims of this phenomenon; when 85 of them were given a random mix of small and large bowls and scoops, those who got larger bowls served themselves 31% more ice cream, and added on another 14.5% if they had bigger scoops!<ref>[http://cat.inist.fr/?aModele=afficheN&cpsidt=18069027 '''Brian Wansink, Koert van Ittersum, and James E. Painter.''' September 2006. Ice Cream Illusions: Bowls, Spoons, and Self-Served Portion Sizes. American Journal of Preventive Medicine. 31(3):240-243]</ref>

# [[Image:Utensils_643.jpg|thumb]]'''Put down the knife.''' By putting down whatever utensils you're using between every bite, you can significantly slow down your eating time, leaving your stomach a chance to feel full and reducing the likelihood that you'll go for seconds. Another technique that can have a similar effect is to [[Drink More Water Every Day|take a sip]] between each bite. Numerous studies have shown that eating slowly results in eating less.<ref>[http://www.livescience.com/health/061115_eating_slow.html Science Confirms Diet Tactic: Eat Slow, Eat Less]</ref> There's even a device you can get from a dentist that you wear to make your oral cavity smaller so that you take smaller bites,<ref name="webmd" /> and a fork that's so awkward to use that you'll get less food per bite!<ref>[http://www.dietfork.com The Diet Fork]</ref>

# [[Image:Oatmealcookies_579.jpg|thumb]]'''Know the enemy!''' Make a list of the food items that are your weaknesses. These aren't always unhealthy foods, either. Sometimes we fool ourselves into believing that as long as we avoid the "bad" foods, we're making progress. At least, that's what we like to think as we get up for our third serving of fruit salad, or finish a bag of pretzels in one sitting, saying that they're healthier than chips. Remember that too much of anything is bad. You probably don't need to keep a [[Keep a Food Diary|food diary]] to know your enemies. Common culprits include [[Quit Soda Pop|soda]], bread, [[Quit Drinking Alcohol|alcohol]], and [[Overcome an Addiction to Fast Food|fast food]]. Whatever your weakness is, cut down on it. If you cut it out completely, you're more likely to binge. Buy only small packages of it and have it only once in a while. If cutting down doesn't work, you might need to go cold turkey.

#[[Image:Wholegrainpasta_466.jpg|thumb|Whole grain pasta]]'''Choose whole grains over a whole belly.''' If you switch out all of your refined grain food (white bread, food made with white flour) for whole-grain food (oatmeal, whole-grain cereal, whole-grain pasta, brown rice and barley) you won't lose additional weight overall. However, you ''will'' lose more weight in the belly area, which will make you look thinner--at least, that's what a Penn State [[Study|study]] implies.<ref name="drweil">http://www.drweil.com/drw/u/QAA400379/Whole-Grains-Shrink-Belly-Fat.html</ref> Not only will your slimmer profile make you feel better about your progress, but by losing the VAT (visceral adipose tissue) you're also doing away with a risk factor for [[Prevent Type 2 Diabetes|type 2 diabetes]], coronary vascular disease, and some types of [[Celebrate Cancer Awareness Month|cancer]].<ref>[http://www.wwltv.com/local/stories/wwl043008mlfarris.b6d54301.html Whole Grains Shrinks Belly Fat]</ref> Check those labels and make sure that any grain-based foods you buy are made up of at least fifty-one percent whole grain.<ref name="drweil" />

# [[Image:Grocerylist_537.jpg|thumb]]'''Limit your spending.''' Some people have an easier time [[Save Money|controlling their wallet]] than controlling their diet. Go ahead, cut up those credit cards, and build up your emergency fund, if you haven't already (in its own account, and leave the bank card at home). Limit the amount of cash you have in your wallet, especially if you're subject to spontaneous fast food indulgences. When you go grocery shopping, have a list prepared, and bring just enough money to cover those items (this might take a few dry runs). The embarrassment of not having enough money at the register will keep you from throwing a few extra items in the shopping cart. If you don't do the grocery shopping, then offer to take on this monumental role. Your family or roommates might complain about the absence of junk food, but you'll be doing them a favor by stocking the kitchen with healthy stuff. They'll thank you...later...years later.

# [[Image:Digitalwatch_476.jpg|thumb]]'''Set a digital watch to go off every two hours.''' Eat only when the watch tells you to. Spontaneous eating sessions (those times when you feel those hunger pangs, those [[Stop Sweet Cravings|cravings]], and you scour the cabinets or the streets in search of satisfaction) are your weakest points. This is why all weight loss books tell you to avoid skipping meals. If you eat every two hours, you won't get so hungry that you gorge yourself when you do eat. You know how it goes: "Oh...I'm so hungry...the brownies are right there...I'd have to walk all the way to the deli to get a sandwich, but my stomach's churning...." Of course, if you eat the equivalent of a cheeseburger every two hours, that's a recipe for obesity, but again, you're more likely to retain self-control and stick to your diet when you don't have hunger pangs to cloud your judgment. It wouldn't hurt, however, to [[Plan Everyday Meals for Your Family|plan out what you'll eat]] (smoothie at 10, chicken salad at 12, a single piece of leftover cherry pie at 2, a slice of bread with peanut butter at 4, and so on).

#*This has the added benefit of [[Increase Your Metabolism|increasing your metabolism]]. Extending the time between meals makes your body go into "starvation mode," which will slow down your [[Increase Your Metabolism|metabolism]] in response to the perceived threat of starvation. This is why fasting and skipping meals will only make things worse. In addition to having four to six small meals per day,<ref>[http://www.webmd.com/diet/features/rev-up-your-metabolism Rev Up Your Metabolism]</ref> eating healthy snacks will also [[Increase Your Metabolism|increase your metabolism]].<ref>[http://www.webmd.com/fitness-exercise/guide/make-most-your-metabolism Make the Most of Your Metabolism]</ref>

#*Another useful way to think about this is to use a "hunger scale." Rate your hunger on a scale of 0 to 10, with 0 being so hungry that you feel weak and 10 being so full that you just want to curl up in bed and digest. Eat when you're at about 3, which is when you're just a little hungry, but not famished.<ref>[http://www.thedietchannel.com/kick-new-year-with-10-tips Kick the New Year Right With These 10 Diet Tips]</ref>

# [[Image:Cash_975.jpg|thumb]]'''Trade weight for cash.''' A 2007 [[Study|study]] showed that the more you pay people to lose weight, the more pounds they drop over a three-month period.<ref>[http://www.joem.org/pt/re/joem/abstract.00043764-200709000-00008.htm;jsessionid=L0GVF1XFGN33yJ8x69T4TLlr6PJ9bkJn2yJF56yvCGQRPNth4CQh!-573288796!181195629!8091!-1 '''Eric A. Finkelstein, Laura A. Linnan, Deborah F. Tate, Ben E. Birken.''' September 2007. A Pilot Study Testing the Effect of Different Levels of Financial Incentives on Weight Loss among Overweight Employees. Journal of Occupational & Environmental Medicine. 49(9):981-989.]</ref> If there's someone who keeps nagging you to lose weight, ask that person about paying you for every pound you lose. If your employer is self-insured, he or she might consider enlisting the services of a company that develops reward programs to encourage employees to lose weight.<ref>[http://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2007/11/10/AR2007111000074_pf.html An Economy of Scales: Paying People to Lose Weight Helps Drop Pounds and Health-Care Costs]</ref> You can also sign a contract that forces you to pay up for every pound you don't lose (or every pound you gain)<ref>[https://stickk.com StickK]</ref> and whatever money you pay (or gain) can be [[Give Charity Donations Safely|donated to charity]].
== Tips ==
<!-- EDITORS: This is a popular topic with many controversial and conflicting theories.  Don't add any information here unless it is referenced to a reliable source.  Read how to

* Keep a fitness log: Get a blank piece of paper and [[Draw|draw]] about forty small squares or print a spreadsheet from Microsoft Excel. Try to figure out your most common exercise-related activities and make two letter (or number) codes for them. Add a few more activities to get you moving. Set a date to complete all of your squares. Consider going over your log daily to fill in the squares, as you will not remember what activity you did three weeks from now. Make sure that your date goals are reasonable and timely.

*[[Image:Salsadancing_620.jpg|thumb|Dancing can be an aerobic workout]]For physical activity, try something different. Maybe you’ve stopped going to the gym because it's boring. Do something unique and preferably something that involves a long-term commitment and contract, such as swing or [[Dance Salsa|salsa dancing]], [[Swim|swimming lessons]], [[Learn to Fence|fencing]], or [[Choose a Martial Art|martial arts]]. Choose a school or instructor you like--you're more likely to show up, especially if there's someone holding you accountable. The more expensive the contract, the more likely you are to stick with it...unless you're filthy rich, in which case you can hire a personal trainer.

*If you are having a hard time getting started or maintaining an exercise routine, use Monday as the day to recommit. Instead of making it a New Year’s Resolution or something you start doing on your birthday, using Monday gives you fifty-two chances to get on track!
== Warnings ==
<!-- EDITORS: This is a popular topic with many controversial and conflicting theories.  Don't add any information here unless it is referenced to a reliable source.  Read how to
http://www.wikihow.com/Reference-Sources-on-wikiHow
to cite any edit you wish to add.  Non referenced information may be deleted quickly.  -->

*Don't over exercise or lose too much weight. Check with your doctor if you are going to start a new and more healthy diet before you begin. Make sure you check your BMI for improvement and make sure you aren't losing too much weight (that's not good). Being underweight is also unhealthy and can increase the risk of osteoporosis. Keep a steady, slowly progressing weight loss status. It will benefit in the long run.

*[[Image:Hospital 4761.jpg|thumb|Consulting the doctor.]]Consult your doctor before making any major changes to your lifestyle if you have a medical condition that could be affected.  Consulting your doctor can also help you rule out medical conditions that could be contributing to your weight.
* Don't lose weight too quickly. The harder you push yourself, the higher the chance of relapse. Slow and steady wins the race.

* Remember that being healthy overall is more important than losing weight. Preventing obesity should be like preventing diabetes or cancer or hypertension; you are preventing a disease. Never do anything unhealthful to lose weight. You don’t want to substitute one disease for another.
* Avoid "fad" diets such as the cabbage soup diet, "carb-loading," boiled egg diet, etc.

# '''Focus on the tried and true.''' Ultimately, losing weight comes down to one key principle: Burn more calories than you consume. The steps that follow won't work if you have a thousand more calories coming into your body on a daily basis than you have going out. Lay the foundation for weight loss with these practices:
#*Count calories and [[Keep a Food Diary|keep a food diary]].
#*[[Keep to Your Diet|Go on a diet.]]
#*Cut down on [[Eat Less Sugar|sugar]], [[Avoid High Fructose Corn Syrup|high fructose corn syrup]], [[Avoid Trans Fats|trans fats]] and [[Limit Your Saturated Fat Intake|saturated fats]].
#* Burn more calories by [[Exercise|exercising]]: [[Run]], [[Walk|walk]], even [[Exercise While Sitting at Your Computer|exercise at the computer]] you are sitting in front of now.
#* [[Increase Your Metabolism|Raise your metabolism.]]

# [[Image:Bowlmaccheese_73.jpg|thumb|Big bowl, big servings, big weight gain]]'''Downsize your kitchenware.''' The human mind works in mysterious ways. It turns out that using smaller bowls, plates, and containers can subconsciously influence how much you serve yourself. Even nutrition experts are victims of this phenomenon; when 85 of them were given a random mix of small and large bowls and scoops, those who got larger bowls served themselves 31% more ice cream, and added on another 14.5% if they had bigger scoops!<ref>[http://cat.inist.fr/?aModele=afficheN&cpsidt=18069027 '''Brian Wansink, Koert van Ittersum, and James E. Painter.''' September 2006. Ice Cream Illusions: Bowls, Spoons, and Self-Served Portion Sizes. American Journal of Preventive Medicine. 31(3):240-243]</ref>

# [[Image:Utensils_643.jpg|thumb]]'''Put down the knife.''' By putting down whatever utensils you're using between every bite, you can significantly slow down your eating time, leaving your stomach a chance to feel full and reducing the likelihood that you'll go for seconds. Another technique that can have a similar effect is to [[Drink More Water Every Day|take a sip]] between each bite. Numerous studies have shown that eating slowly results in eating less.<ref>[http://www.livescience.com/health/061115_eating_slow.html Science Confirms Diet Tactic: Eat Slow, Eat Less]</ref> There's even a device you can get from a dentist that you wear to make your oral cavity smaller so that you take smaller bites,<ref name="webmd" /> and a fork that's so awkward to use that you'll get less food per bite!<ref>[http://www.dietfork.com The Diet Fork]</ref>

# [[Image:Oatmealcookies_579.jpg|thumb]]'''Know the enemy''' Make a list of the food items that are your weaknesses. These aren't always unhealthy foods, either. Sometimes we fool ourselves into believing that as long as we avoid the "bad" foods, we're making progress. At least, that's what we like to think as we get up for our third serving of fruit salad, or finish a bag of pretzels in one sitting, saying that they're healthier than chips. Remember that too much of anything is bad. You probably don't need to keep a [[Keep a Food Diary|food diary]] to know your enemies. Common culprits include [[Quit Soda Pop|soda]], bread, [[Quit Drinking Alcohol|alcohol]], and [[Overcome an Addiction to Fast Food|fast food]]. Whatever your weakness is, cut down on it. If you cut it out completely, you're more likely to binge. Buy only small packages of it and have it only once in a while. If cutting down doesn't work, you might need to go cold turkey.

#[[Image:Wholegrainpasta_466.jpg|thumb|Whole grain pasta]]'''Choose whole grains over a whole belly.''' If you switch out all of your refined grain food (white bread, food made with white flour) for whole-grain food (oatmeal, whole-grain cereal, whole-grain pasta, brown rice and barley) you won't lose additional weight overall. However, you ''will'' lose more weight in the belly area, which will make you look thinner--at least, that's what a Penn State [[Study|study]] implies.<ref name="drweil">http://www.drweil.com/drw/u/QAA400379/Whole-Grains-Shrink-Belly-Fat.html</ref> Not only will your slimmer profile make you feel better about your progress, but by losing the VAT (visceral adipose tissue) you're also doing away with a risk factor for [[Prevent Type 2 Diabetes|type 2 diabetes]], coronary vascular disease, and some types of [[Celebrate Cancer Awareness Month|cancer]].<ref>[http://www.wwltv.com/local/stories/wwl043008mlfarris.b6d54301.html Whole Grains Shrinks Belly Fat]</ref> Check those labels and make sure that any grain-based foods you buy are made up of at least fifty-one percent whole grain.<ref name="drweil" />

# [[Image:Grocerylist_537.jpg|thumb]]'''Limit your spending.''' Some people have an easier time [[Save Money|controlling their wallet]] than controlling their diet. Go ahead, cut up those credit cards, and build up your emergency fund, if you haven't already (in its own account, and leave the bank card at home). Limit the amount of cash you have in your wallet, especially if you're subject to spontaneous fast food indulgences. When you go grocery shopping, have a list prepared, and bring just enough money to cover those items (this might take a few dry runs). The embarrassment of not having enough money at the register will keep you from throwing a few extra items in the shopping cart. If you don't do the grocery shopping, then offer to take on this monumental role. Your family or roommates might complain about the absence of junk food, but you'll be doing them a favor by stocking the kitchen with healthy stuff. They'll thank you...later...years later.

# [[Image:Digitalwatch_476.jpg|thumb]]'''Set a digital watch to go off every two hours.''' Eat only when the watch tells you to. Spontaneous eating sessions (those times when you feel those hunger pangs, those [[Stop Sweet Cravings|cravings]], and you scour the cabinets or the streets in search of satisfaction) are your weakest points. This is why all weight loss books tell you to avoid skipping meals. If you eat every two hours, you won't get so hungry that you gorge yourself when you do eat. You know how it goes: "Oh...I'm so hungry...the brownies are right there...I'd have to walk all the way to the deli to get a sandwich, but my stomach's churning...." Of course, if you eat the equivalent of a cheeseburger every two hours, that's a recipe for obesity, but again, you're more likely to retain self-control and stick to your diet when you don't have hunger pangs to cloud your judgment. It wouldn't hurt, however, to [[Plan Everyday Meals for Your Family|plan out what you'll eat]] (smoothie at 10, chicken salad at 12, a single piece of leftover cherry pie at 2, a slice of bread with peanut butter at 4, and so on).

#*This has the added benefit of [[Increase Your Metabolism|increasing your metabolism]]. Extending the time between meals makes your body go into "starvation mode," which will slow down your metabolism in response to the perceived threat of starvation. This is why fasting and skipping meals will only make things worse. In addition to having four to six small meals per day,<ref>[http://www.webmd.com/diet/features/rev-up-your-metabolism Rev Up Your Metabolism]</ref> eating healthy snacks will also [[Increase Your Metabolism|increase your metabolism]].<ref>[http://www.webmd.com/fitness-exercise/guide/make-most-your-metabolism Make the Most of Your Metabolism]</ref>

#*Another useful way to think about this is to use a "hunger scale." Rate your hunger on a scale of 0 to 10, with 0 being so hungry that you feel weak and 10 being so full that you just want to curl up in bed and digest. Eat when you're at about 3, which is when you're just a little hungry, but not famished.<ref>[http://www.thedietchannel.com/kick-new-year-with-10-tips Kick the New Year Right With These 10 Diet Tips]</ref>

# [[Image:Cash_975.jpg|thumb]]'''Trade weight for cash.''' A 2007 [[Study|study]] showed that the more you pay people to lose weight, the more pounds they drop over a three-month period.<ref>[http://www.joem.org/pt/re/joem/abstract.00043764-200709000-00008.htm;jsessionid=L0GVF1XFGN33yJ8x69T4TLlr6PJ9bkJn2yJF56yvCGQRPNth4CQh!-573288796!181195629!8091!-1 '''Eric A. Finkelstein, Laura A. Linnan, Deborah F. Tate, Ben E. Birken.''' September 2007. A Pilot Study Testing the Effect of Different Levels of Financial Incentives on Weight Loss among Overweight Employees. Journal of Occupational & Environmental Medicine. 49(9):981-989.]</ref> If there's someone who keeps nagging you to lose weight, ask that person about paying you for every pound you lose. If your employer is self-insured, he or she might consider enlisting the services of a company that develops reward programs to encourage employees to lose weight.<ref>[http://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2007/11/10/AR2007111000074_pf.html An Economy of Scales: Paying People to Lose Weight Helps Drop Pounds and Health-Care Costs]</ref> You can also sign a contract that forces you to pay up for every pound you don't lose (or every pound you gain)<ref>[https://stickk.com StickK]</ref> and whatever money you pay (or gain) can be [[Give Charity Donations Safely|donated to charity]].

* Keep a fitness log: Get a blank piece of paper and [[Draw|draw]] about forty small squares or print a spreadsheet from Microsoft Excel. Try to figure out your most common exercise-related activities and make two letter (or number) codes for them. Add a few more activities to get you moving. Set a date to complete all of your squares. Consider going over your log daily to fill in the squares, as you will not remember what activity you did three weeks from now. Make sure that your date goals are reasonable and timely.

*[[Image:Salsadancing_620.jpg|thumb|Dancing can be an aerobic workout]]For physical activity, try something different. Maybe you’ve stopped going to the gym because it's boring. Do something unique and preferably something that involves a long-term commitment and contract, such as swing or [[Dance Salsa|salsa dancing]], [[Swim|swimming lessons]], [[Learn to Fence|fencing]], or [[Choose a Martial Art|martial arts]]. Choose a school or instructor you like--you're more likely to show up, especially if there's someone holding you accountable. The more expensive the contract, the more likely you are to stick with it...unless you're filthy rich, in which case you can hire a personal trainer.

*If you are having a hard time getting started or maintaining an exercise routine, use Monday as the day to recommit. Instead of making it a New Year’s Resolution or something you start doing on your birthday, using Monday gives you fifty-two chances to get on track!

*You can also look at weight lose products.  The Acai Berry Actives Program helps you lose weight by increasing your metabolism and fat oxidation,fighting fatique, increasing energy, and is also a powerful antioxidant support.  It has a free trial offer with money back guarantee.  Check it out:[www.undoweight.com].
== Warnings ==
<!-- EDITORS: This is a popular topic with many controversial and conflicting theories.  Don't add any information here unless it is referenced to a reliable source.  Read how to
http://www.wikihow.com/Reference-Sources-on-wikiHow
to cite any edit you wish to add.  Non referenced information may be deleted quickly.  -->

*Don't over exercise or lose too much weight. Check with your doctor if you are going to start a new and more healthy diet before you begin. Make sure you check your BMI for improvement and make sure you aren't losing too much weight (that's not good). Being underweight is also unhealthy and can increase the risk of osteoporosis. Keep a steady, slowly progressing weight loss status. It will benefit in the long run.

*[[Image:Hospital 4761.jpg|thumb|Consulting the doctor.]]Consult your doctor before making any major changes to your lifestyle if you have a medical condition that could be affected.  Consulting your doctor can also help you rule out medical conditions that could be contributing to your weight.
* Don't lose weight too quickly. The harder you push yourself, the higher the chance of relapse. Slow and steady wins the race.

* Remember that being healthy overall is more important than losing weight. Preventing obesity should be like preventing diabetes or cancer or hypertension; you are preventing a disease. Never do anything unhealthful to lose weight. You don’t want to substitute one disease for another.
* Avoid "fad" diets such as the cabbage soup diet, "carb-loading," boiled egg diet, etc.

# [[Image:Grocerylist_537.jpg|thumb]]'''Limit your spending.''' Some people have an easier time [[Save Money|controlling their wallet]] than controlling their diet. Go ahead, cut up those credit cards, and build up your emergency fund, if you haven't already (in its own account, and leave the bank card at home). Limit the amount of cash you have in your wallet, especially if you're subject to spontaneous fast food indulgences. When you go grocery shopping, have a list prepared, and bring just enough money to cover those items (this might take a few dry runs). The embarrassment of not having enough money at the register will keep you from throwing a few extra items in the shopping cart. If you don't do the grocery shopping, then offer to take on this monumental role. Your family or roommates might complain about the absence of junk food, but you'll be doing them a favor by stocking the kitchen with healthy stuff. They'll thank you...later...years later.

# [[Image:Digitalwatch_476.jpg|thumb]]'''Set a digital watch to go off every two hours.''' Eat only when the watch tells you to. Spontaneous eating sessions (those times when you feel those hunger pangs, those [[Stop Sweet Cravings|cravings]], and you scour the cabinets or the streets in search of satisfaction) are your weakest points. This is why all weight loss books tell you to avoid skipping meals. If you eat every two hours, you won't get so hungry that you gorge yourself when you do eat. You know how it goes: "Oh...I'm so hungry...the brownies are right there...I'd have to walk all the way to the deli to get a sandwich, but my stomach's churning...." Of course, if you eat the equivalent of a cheeseburger every two hours, that's a recipe for obesity, but again, you're more likely to retain self-control and stick to your diet when you don't have hunger pangs to cloud your judgment. It wouldn't hurt, however, to [[Plan Everyday Meals for Your Family|plan out what you'll eat]] (smoothie at 10, chicken salad at 12, a single piece of leftover cherry pie at 2, a slice of bread with peanut butter at 4, and so on).

#*This has the added benefit of [[Increase Your Metabolism|increasing your metabolism]]. Extending the time between meals makes your body go into "starvation mode," which will slow down your metabolism in response to the perceived threat of starvation. This is why fasting and skipping meals will only make things worse. In addition to having four to six small meals per day,<ref>[http://www.webmd.com/diet/features/rev-up-your-metabolism Rev Up Your Metabolism]</ref> eating healthy snacks will also [[Increase Your Metabolism|increase your metabolism]].<ref>[http://www.webmd.com/fitness-exercise/guide/make-most-your-metabolism Make the Most of Your Metabolism]</ref>

#*Another useful way to think about this is to use a "hunger scale." Rate your hunger on a scale of 0 to 10, with 0 being so hungry that you feel weak and 10 being so full that you just want to curl up in bed and digest. Eat when you're at about 3, which is when you're just a little hungry, but not famished.<ref>[http://www.thedietchannel.com/kick-new-year-with-10-tips Kick the New Year Right With These 10 Diet Tips]</ref>

# [[Image:Cash_975.jpg|thumb]]'''Trade weight for cash.''' A 2007 [[Study|study]] showed that the more you pay people to lose weight, the more pounds they drop over a three-month period.<ref>[http://www.joem.org/pt/re/joem/abstract.00043764-200709000-00008.htm;jsessionid=L0GVF1XFGN33yJ8x69T4TLlr6PJ9bkJn2yJF56yvCGQRPNth4CQh!-573288796!181195629!8091!-1 '''Eric A. Finkelstein, Laura A. Linnan, Deborah F. Tate, Ben E. Birken.''' September 2007. A Pilot Study Testing the Effect of Different Levels of Financial Incentives on Weight Loss among Overweight Employees. Journal of Occupational & Environmental Medicine. 49(9):981-989.]</ref> If there's someone who keeps nagging you to lose weight, ask that person about paying you for every pound you lose. If your employer is self-insured, he or she might consider enlisting the services of a company that develops reward programs to encourage employees to lose weight.<ref>[http://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2007/11/10/AR2007111000074_pf.html An Economy of Scales: Paying People to Lose Weight Helps Drop Pounds and Health-Care Costs]</ref> You can also sign a contract that forces you to pay up for every pound you don't lose (or every pound you gain)<ref>[https://stickk.com StickK]</ref> and whatever money you pay (or gain) can be [[Give Charity Donations Safely|donated to charity]].

* Keep a fitness log: Get a blank piece of paper and [[Draw|draw]] about forty small squares or print a spreadsheet from Microsoft Excel. Try to figure out your most common exercise-related activities and make two letter (or number) codes for them. Add a few more activities to get you moving. Set a date to complete all of your squares. Consider going over your log daily to fill in the squares, as you will not remember what activity you did three weeks from now. Make sure that your date goals are reasonable and timely.

*[[Image:Salsadancing_620.jpg|thumb|Dancing can be an aerobic workout]]For physical activity, try something different. Maybe you’ve stopped going to the gym because it's boring. Do something unique and preferably something that involves a long-term commitment and contract, such as swing or [[Dance Salsa|salsa dancing]], [[Swim|swimming lessons]], [[Learn to Fence|fencing]], or [[Choose a Martial Art|martial arts]]. Choose a school or instructor you like--you're more likely to show up, especially if there's someone holding you accountable. The more expensive the contract, the more likely you are to stick with it...unless you're filthy rich, in which case you can hire a personal trainer.

*If you are having a hard time getting started or maintaining an exercise routine, use Monday as the day to recommit. Instead of making it a New Year’s Resolution or something you start doing on your birthday, using Monday gives you fifty-two chances to get on track!

*Don't over exercise or lose too much weight. Check with your doctor if you are going to start a new and more healthy diet before you begin. Make sure you check your BMI for improvement and make sure you aren't losing too much weight (that's not good). Being underweight is also unhealthy and can increase the risk of osteoporosis. Keep a steady, slowly progressing weight loss status. It will benefit in the long run.

*[[Image:Hospital 4761.jpg|thumb|Consulting the doctor.]]Consult your doctor before making any major changes to your lifestyle if you have a medical condition that could be affected.  Consulting your doctor can also help you rule out medical conditions that could be contributing to your weight.
* Don't lose weight too quickly. The harder you push yourself, the higher the chance of relapse. Slow and steady wins the race.

* Remember that being healthy overall is more important than losing weight. Preventing obesity should be like preventing diabetes or cancer or hypertension; you are preventing a disease. Never do anything unhealthful to lose weight. You don’t want to substitute one disease for another.
* Avoid "fad" diets such as the cabbage soup diet, "carb-loading," boiled egg diet, etc.

removed: Most weight loss counselors instruct people to follow a specific "daily calorie limit" which is based on their weight & height (and sometimes their activity level is factored in too).
For example, some weight loss counselors may tell you to eat 2,000 calories per day if you weigh a certain amount (and if you describe yourself as "active").
But this is a RIDICULOUS way to try and lose weight, and we'll explain why below.
The truth is that it's quite ridiculous to follow a specific calorie limit each day, since every person has a different metabolism level.

You cannot judge your metabolism by your activity level either, since there are plenty of people with higher activity levels but who are overweight nonetheless (due to a slower than normal metabolism).

For example, if you take 2 people who weigh 165 lbs and who have the same activity level each day, then there is no guarantee that their metabolisms will be operating at the same general level.  In fact, it's quite possible that one person's metabolism will be nearly twice as fast as the other person's metabolism.

You see, your body doesn't burn calories on a "per day" basis, your body burns calories on a "per meal" basis.  Your body doesn't burn calories based on what time the sun rises and sets, it burns calories throughout the day as you eat them.

This means that following some arbitrary "daily caloric guideline" is not going to make you any thinner, since you must actually learn to spread out your daily food across more than 3 meals per day in order to lose weight fast. In fact, people who count calories usually fail at weight loss, and that's because counting calories doesn't work.

Go check out the new Online Diet Generator at http://www.WeightLossOrg.com, an 11 day menu which allows you to eat more than 3 meals per day and it also allows you to eat until you feel satisfied (no specific calorie limits are needed).

Fat is used in cellular membranes and enables the body to absorb fat-soluble vitamins, including vitamins A and D. Good fats such as olive oil or the fat in nuts may reduce the risk of heart disease by benefiting lipid profiles and unclogging arteries.

Carbohydrates are ''used'' for one purpose: energy--burning carbohydrates for energy. Some excess carbohydrates are turned into glycogen and stored in the liver, then if there is more than the liver can retain, then it is converted to body fat. Carbohydrates raise blood sugar and stimulate the production of insulin, a hormone that transports glucose to fat cells for storage; fats and proteins can be used for energy without a raise in blood sugar. Nutritionists have the glycemic index to measure how quickly foods increase blood sugar. Foods without carbs do '''not''' raise blood sugar and aren’t even assigned GI values. “There are no GI values given for meat, poultry, fish, avocados, salad vegetables, cheese, or eggs because these foods contain little or no carbohydrate and it would be exceedingly difficult for people to consume a portion of the foods containing 50 g or even 25 g of available carbohydrate. Even in large amounts, these foods when eaten alone are not likely to induce a significant rise in blood glucose.”[http://www.ajcn.org/cgi/content/full/76/1/5 '''Kaye Foster-Powell, Susanna H. A. Holt, and Janette C. Brand-Miller.''' July 2002. International Table of Glycemic Index and Glycemic Load Values: 2002. American Journal of Clinical Nutrition 76(1):5-56]

Carbohydrates are '''not''' necessary for life; when in ketosis, the body produces glucose from protein. This is healthy in the long-term and the most effective way to lose weight, provided you make it a lifetime commitment. Constantly switching from carbs to no carbs and back is more dangerous than just eating the carbs and staying fat.
*Don't look up to celebrities for their diets.The chemical diets ''will not'' work. All of us want to keep fit, but most of all healthy.

{{fa}}[[Image:Lostweight_94.jpg|200px|right]]



You already know that to lose weight, you need to burn more calories than you consume. You've tried [[Lose Weight By Dieting|dieting]], keeping a [[Keep a Food Diary|food diary]], creating an [[Start Your Own Exercise Regimen and Stick to It|exercise regimen]], and perhaps even [[Find a Hypnotherapist|hypnosis]]. It's now obvious that the problem isn't with the technique, but with your [[Have Willpower|willpower]]. Old [[Break a Habit|habits]] die hard. If you're having a hard time maintaining your efforts over time, here are some radical ways to break away from the routine.
[[Category:Losing Weight]]

== Steps ==
<!-- EDITORS: This is a popular topic with many controversial and conflicting theories.  Don't add any information here unless it is referenced to a reliable source.  Read how to
http://www.wikihow.com/Reference-Sources-on-wikiHow
to cite any edit you wish to add.  Non referenced information may be deleted quickly.  -->
<!-- EDITORS: This first step should be concise.  Just link to full articles, rather than writing whole sentences. -->

# '''Focus on the tried and true.''' Ultimately, losing weight comes down to one key principle: Burn more calories than you consume. The steps that follow won't work if you have a thousand more calories coming into your body on a daily basis than you have going out. Lay the foundation for weight loss with these practices:
#*Count calories and [[Keep a Food Diary|keep a food diary]].
#*[[Keep to Your Diet|Go on a diet.]]
#*Cut down on [[Eat Less Sugar|sugar]], [[Avoid High Fructose Corn Syrup|high fructose corn syrup]], [[Avoid Trans Fats|trans fats]] and [[Limit Your Saturated Fat Intake|saturated fats]].
#* Burn more calories by [[Exercise|exercising]]: [[Run]], [[Walk|walk]], even [[Exercise While Sitting at Your Computer|exercise at the computer]] you are sitting in front of now.
#* [[Increase Your Metabolism|Raise your metabolism.]]

# [[Image:Bowlmaccheese_73.jpg|thumb|Big bowl, big servings, big weight gain]]'''Downsize your kitchenware.''' The human mind works in mysterious ways. It turns out that using smaller bowls, plates, and containers can subconsciously influence how much you serve yourself. Even nutrition experts are victims of this phenomenon; when 85 of them were given a random mix of small and large bowls and scoops, those who got larger bowls served themselves 31% more ice cream, and added on another 14.5% if they had bigger scoops!<ref>[http://cat.inist.fr/?aModele=afficheN&cpsidt=18069027 '''Brian Wansink, Koert van Ittersum, and James E. Painter.''' September 2006. Ice Cream Illusions: Bowls, Spoons, and Self-Served Portion Sizes. American Journal of Preventive Medicine. 31(3):240-243]</ref>

# [[Image:Utensils_643.jpg|thumb]]'''Put down the knife.''' By putting down whatever utensils you're using between every bite, you can significantly slow down your eating time, leaving your stomach a chance to feel full and reducing the likelihood that you'll go for seconds. Another technique that can have a similar effect is to [[Drink More Water Every Day|take a sip]] between each bite. Numerous studies have shown that eating slowly results in eating less.<ref>[http://www.livescience.com/health/061115_eating_slow.html Science Confirms Diet Tactic: Eat Slow, Eat Less]</ref> There's even a device you can get from a dentist that you wear to make your oral cavity smaller so that you take smaller bites,<ref name="webmd" /> and a fork that's so awkward to use that you'll get less food per bite!<ref>[http://www.dietfork.com The Diet Fork]</ref>

# [[Image:Oatmealcookies_579.jpg|thumb]]'''Know the enemy''' Make a list of the food items that are your weaknesses. These aren't always unhealthy foods, either. Sometimes we fool ourselves into believing that as long as we avoid the "bad" foods, we're making progress. At least, that's what we like to think as we get up for our third serving of fruit salad, or finish a bag of pretzels in one sitting, saying that they're healthier than chips. Remember that too much of anything is bad. You probably don't need to keep a [[Keep a Food Diary|food diary]] to know your enemies. Common culprits include [[Quit Soda Pop|soda]], bread, [[Quit Drinking Alcohol|alcohol]], and [[Overcome an Addiction to Fast Food|fast food]]. Whatever your weakness is, cut down on it. If you cut it out completely, you're more likely to binge. Buy only small packages of it and have it only once in a while. If cutting down doesn't work, you might need to go cold turkey.

#[[Image:Wholegrainpasta_466.jpg|thumb|Whole grain pasta]]'''Choose whole grains over a whole belly.''' If you switch out all of your refined grain food (white bread, food made with white flour) for whole-grain food (oatmeal, whole-grain cereal, whole-grain pasta, brown rice and barley) you won't lose additional weight overall. However, you ''will'' lose more weight in the belly area, which will make you look thinner--at least, that's what a Penn State study implies.<ref name="drweil">http://www.drweil.com/drw/u/QAA400379/Whole-Grains-Shrink-Belly-Fat.html</ref> Not only will your slimmer profile make you feel better about your progress, but by losing the VAT (visceral adipose tissue) you're also doing away with a risk factor for [[Prevent Type 2 Diabetes|type 2 diabetes]], coronary vascular disease, and some types of [[Celebrate Cancer Awareness Month|cancer]].<ref>[http://www.wwltv.com/local/stories/wwl043008mlfarris.b6d54301.html Whole Grains Shrinks Belly Fat]</ref> Check those labels and make sure that any grain-based foods you buy are made up of at least fifty-one percent whole grain.<ref name="drweil" />

# [[Image:Grocerylist_537.jpg|thumb]]'''Limit your spending.''' Some people have an easier time [[Save Money|controlling their wallet]] than controlling their diet. Go ahead, cut up those credit cards, and build up your emergency fund, if you haven't already (in its own account, and leave the bank card at home). Limit the amount of cash you have in your wallet, especially if you're subject to spontaneous fast food indulgences. When you go grocery shopping, have a list prepared, and bring just enough money to cover those items (this might take a few dry runs). The embarrassment of not having enough money at the register will keep you from throwing a few extra items in the shopping cart. If you don't do the grocery shopping, then offer to take on this monumental role. Your family or roommates might complain about the absence of junk food, but you'll be doing them a favor by stocking the kitchen with healthy stuff. They'll thank you...later...years later.

# [[Image:Digitalwatch_476.jpg|thumb]]'''Set a digital watch to go off every two hours.''' Eat only when the watch tells you to. Spontaneous eating sessions (those times when you feel those hunger pangs, those [[Stop Sweet Cravings|cravings]], and you scour the cabinets or the streets in search of satisfaction) are your weakest points. This is why all weight loss books tell you to avoid skipping meals. If you eat every two hours, you won't get so hungry that you gorge yourself when you do eat. You know how it goes: "Oh...I'm so hungry...the brownies are right there...I'd have to walk all the way to the deli to get a sandwich, but my stomach's churning...." Of course, if you eat the equivalent of a cheeseburger every two hours, that's a recipe for obesity, but again, you're more likely to retain self-control and stick to your diet when you don't have hunger pangs to cloud your judgment. It wouldn't hurt, however, to [[Plan Everyday Meals for Your Family|plan out what you'll eat]] (smoothie at 10, chicken salad at 12, a single piece of leftover cherry pie at 2, a slice of bread with peanut butter at 4, and so on).

#*This has the added benefit of [[Increase Your Metabolism|increasing your metabolism]]. Extending the time between meals makes your body go into "starvation mode," which will slow down your metabolism in response to the perceived threat of starvation. This is why fasting and skipping meals will only make things worse. In addition to having four to six small meals per day,<ref>[http://www.webmd.com/diet/features/rev-up-your-metabolism Rev Up Your Metabolism]</ref> eating healthy snacks will also increase your metabolism.<ref>[http://www.webmd.com/fitness-exercise/guide/make-most-your-metabolism Make the Most of Your Metabolism]</ref>

#*Another useful way to think about this is to use a "hunger scale." Rate your hunger on a scale of 0 to 10, with 0 being so hungry that you feel weak and 10 being so full that you just want to curl up in bed and digest. Eat when you're at about 3, which is when you're just a little hungry, but not famished.<ref>[http://www.thedietchannel.com/kick-new-year-with-10-tips Kick the New Year Right With These 10 Diet Tips]</ref>

# [[Image:Cash_975.jpg|thumb]]'''Trade weight for cash.''' A 2007 study showed that the more you pay people to lose weight, the more pounds they drop over a three-month period.<ref>[http://www.joem.org/pt/re/joem/abstract.00043764-200709000-00008.htm;jsessionid=L0GVF1XFGN33yJ8x69T4TLlr6PJ9bkJn2yJF56yvCGQRPNth4CQh!-573288796!181195629!8091!-1 '''Eric A. Finkelstein, Laura A. Linnan, Deborah F. Tate, Ben E. Birken.''' September 2007. A Pilot Study Testing the Effect of Different Levels of Financial Incentives on Weight Loss among Overweight Employees. Journal of Occupational & Environmental Medicine. 49(9):981-989.]</ref> If there's someone who keeps nagging you to lose weight, ask that person about paying you for every pound you lose. If your employer is self-insured, he or she might consider enlisting the services of a company that develops reward programs to encourage employees to lose weight.<ref>[http://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2007/11/10/AR2007111000074_pf.html An Economy of Scales: Paying People to Lose Weight Helps Drop Pounds and Health-Care Costs]</ref> You can also sign a contract that forces you to pay up for every pound you don't lose (or every pound you gain)<ref>[https://stickk.com StickK]</ref> and whatever money you pay (or gain) can be [[Give Charity Donations Safely|donated to charity]].

# '''Exercise and Save $$$ at the same time''' Walk to the store or library. Whenever your destination is close enough (half a mile one way is enough, especially if you are going to push or carry groceries) Drive only if you are planning to go more than a mile one way or when the weather isn't good.
== Video ==
{{Video:Lose Weight}}
== Tips ==
<!-- EDITORS: This is a popular topic with many controversial and conflicting theories.  Don't add any information here unless it is referenced to a reliable source.  Read how to
http://www.wikihow.com/Reference-Sources-on-wikiHow
to cite any edit you wish to add.  Non referenced information may be deleted quickly.  -->
* You don't have to put on sweats and sneakers or hit the gym to lose weight. You can do some garden work and vacuum the floor on your own property. Picking up toys is good exercise, too.

* Keep a fitness log: Get a blank piece of paper and draw about forty small squares or print a spreadsheet from Microsoft Excel a spreadsheet. Try to figure out your most common exercise-related activities and make two letter (or number) codes for them. Add a few more activities to get you moving. Set a date to complete all of your squares. Consider going over your log daily to fill in the squares, as you will not remember what activity you did three weeks from now. Make sure that your date goals are reasonable and timely.

*[[Image:Salsadancing_620.jpg|thumb|Dancing can be an aerobic workout]]For physical activity, try something different. Maybe you’ve stopped going to the gym because it's boring. Do something unique and preferably something that involves a long-term commitment and contract, such as swing or [[Dance Salsa|salsa dancing]], [[Swim|swimming lessons]], [[Learn to Fence|fencing]], or [[Choose a Martial Art|martial arts]]. Choose a school or instructor you like--you're more likely to show up, especially if there's someone holding you accountable. The more expensive the contract, the more likely you are to stick with it...unless you're filthy rich, in which case you can hire a personal trainer.

*If you are having a hard time getting started or maintaining an exercise routine, use Monday as the day to recommit. Instead of making it a New Year’s Resolution or something you start doing on your birthday, using Monday gives you fifty-two chances to get on track!
*To lose weight<ref>[http://www.101diettips.com/ Lose Weight from 101diettips.com]</ref> consistently, take the stairs instead of escalators and elevators and take brisk walks everyday.
*Follow a simple program that includes a easy to follow meal plan, exercise plan and supplement plan.
== Warnings ==
<!-- EDITORS: This is a popular topic with many controversial and conflicting theories.  Don't add any information here unless it is referenced to a reliable source.  Read how to
http://www.wikihow.com/Reference-Sources-on-wikiHow
to cite any edit you wish to add.  Non referenced information may be deleted quickly.  -->

*Don't over exercise or lose too much weight. Check with your doctor if you are going to start a new and more healthy diet before you begin. Make sure you check your BMI for improvement and make sure you aren't losing too much weight (that's not good). Being underweight is also unhealthy and can increase the risk of osteoporosis.

*[[Image:Hospital 4761.jpg|thumb|Consulting the doctor.]]Consult your doctor before making any major changes to your lifestyle if you have a medical condition that could be affected.  Consulting your doctor can also help you rule out medical conditions that could be contributing to your weight.
* Don't lose weight too quickly. The harder you push yourself, the higher the chance of relapse. Slow and steady wins the race.

* Remember that being healthy overall is more important than losing weight. Preventing obesity should be like preventing diabetes or cancer or hypertension; you are preventing a disease. Never do anything unhealthful to lose weight. You don’t want to substitute one disease for another.

* Avoid "fad" diets such as the cabbage soup diet, "carb-loading," boiled egg diet, etc. Your body requires essential fats and essential amino acids (from proteins) for its bodily processes, but carbohydrates are '''not''' strictly essential because fats and proteins will be changed into glucose in ketosis through the Krebs Cycle (also called the Citric Acid Cycle)[http://porpax.bio.miami.edu/~cmallery/255/255atp/mcb6e.12.1b.jpg diagram of some Molecular Cell Biology] at the cellular mitochondrial level as part of the oxidative process of producing energy.[http://porpax.bio.miami.edu/~cmallery/255/255atp/255makeatp.htm Krebs as part of respiration, energy creation] Protein is used to build muscles, repair cells, and make hormones, such as thyroxine from tyrosine or serotonin from tryptophan. Fat is used in cellular membranes and enables the body to absorb fat-soluble vitamins, including vitamins A and D. Good fats such as olive oil or the fat in nuts may reduce the risk of heart disease by benefiting lipid profiles and unclogging arteries.

Carbohydrates are ''used'' for one purpose: energy--burning carbohydrates for energy. Some excess carbohydrates are turned into glycogen and stored in the liver, then if there is more than the liver can retain, then it is converted to body fat. Carbohydrates raise blood sugar and stimulate the production of insulin, a hormone that transports glucose to fat cells for storage; fats and proteins can be used for energy without a raise in blood sugar. Nutritionists have the glycemic index to measure how quickly foods increase blood sugar. Foods without carbs do '''not''' raise blood sugar and aren’t even assigned GI values. “There are no GI values given for meat, poultry, fish, avocados, salad vegetables, cheese, or eggs because these foods contain little or no carbohydrate and it would be exceedingly difficult for people to consume a portion of the foods containing 50 g or even 25 g of available carbohydrate. Even in large amounts, these foods when eaten alone are not likely to induce a significant rise in blood glucose.”[http://www.ajcn.org/cgi/content/full/76/1/5 '''Kaye Foster-Powell, Susanna H. A. Holt, and Janette C. Brand-Miller.''' July 2002. International Table of Glycemic Index and Glycemic Load Values: 2002. American Journal of Clinical Nutrition 76(1):5-56]

Carbohydrates are '''not''' necessary for life; when in ketosis, the body produces glucose from protein. This is healthy in the long-term and the most effective way to lose weight, provided you make it a lifetime commitment. Constantly switching from carbs to no carbs and back is more dangerous than just eating the carbs and staying fat.
*Don't look up to celebrities for their diets.The chemical diets ''will not'' work. All of us want to keep fit, but most of all healthy.

This is why all weight loss books tell you to avoid skipping meals. If you eat every two hours, you won't get so hungry that you gorge yourself when you do eat. You know how it goes: "Oh...I'm so hungry...the brownies are right there...I'd have to walk all the way to the deli to get a sandwich, but my stomach's churning...." Of course, if you eat the equivalent of a cheeseburger every two hours, that's a recipe for obesity, but again, you're more likely to retain self-control and stick to your diet when you don't have hunger pangs to cloud your judgment. It wouldn't hurt, however, to [[Plan Everyday Meals for Your Family|plan out what you'll eat]] (smoothie at 10, chicken salad at 12, a single piece of leftover cherry pie at 2, a slice of bread with peanut butter at 4, and so on).

#*This has the added benefit of [[Increase Your Metabolism|increasing your metabolism]]. Extending the time between meals makes your body go into "starvation mode," which will slow down your metabolism in response to the perceived threat of starvation. This is why fasting and skipping meals will only make things worse. In addition to having four to six small meals per day,<ref>[http://www.webmd.com/diet/features/rev-up-your-metabolism Rev Up Your Metabolism]</ref> eating healthy snacks will also increase your metabolism.<ref>[http://www.webmd.com/fitness-exercise/guide/make-most-your-metabolism Make the Most of Your Metabolism]</ref>

#*Another useful way to think about this is to use a "hunger scale." Rate your hunger on a scale of 0 to 10, with 0 being so hungry that you feel weak and 10 being so full that you just want to curl up in bed and digest. Eat when you're at about 3, which is when you're just a little hungry, but not famished.<ref>[http://www.thedietchannel.com/kick-new-year-with-10-tips Kick the New Year Right With These 10 Diet Tips]</ref>

# [[Image:Cash_975.jpg|thumb]]'''Trade weight for cash.''' A 2007 study showed that the more you pay people to lose weight, the more pounds they drop over a three-month period.<ref>[http://www.joem.org/pt/re/joem/abstract.00043764-200709000-00008.htm;jsessionid=L0GVF1XFGN33yJ8x69T4TLlr6PJ9bkJn2yJF56yvCGQRPNth4CQh!-573288796!181195629!8091!-1 '''Eric A. Finkelstein, Laura A. Linnan, Deborah F. Tate, Ben E. Birken.''' September 2007. A Pilot Study Testing the Effect of Different Levels of Financial Incentives on Weight Loss among Overweight Employees. Journal of Occupational & Environmental Medicine. 49(9):981-989.]</ref> If there's someone who keeps nagging you to lose weight, ask that person about paying you for every pound you lose. If your employer is self-insured, he or she might consider enlisting the services of a company that develops reward programs to encourage employees to lose weight.<ref>[http://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2007/11/10/AR2007111000074_pf.html An Economy of Scales: Paying People to Lose Weight Helps Drop Pounds and Health-Care Costs]</ref> You can also sign a contract that forces you to pay up for every pound you don't lose (or every pound you gain)<ref>[https://stickk.com StickK]</ref> and whatever money you pay (or gain) can be [[Give Charity Donations Safely|donated to charity]].

# '''Exercise and Save $$$ at the same time''' Walk to the store or library. Whenever your destination is close enough (half a mile one way is enough, especially if you are going to push or carry groceries) Drive only if you are planning to go more than a mile one way or when the weather isn't good.

* You don't have to put on sweats and sneakers or hit the gym to lose weight. You can do some garden work and vacuum the floor on your own property. Picking up toys is good exercise, too.

* Keep a fitness log: Get a blank piece of paper and draw about forty small squares or print a spreadsheet from Microsoft Excel a spreadsheet. Try to figure out your most common exercise-related activities and make two letter (or number) codes for them. Add a few more activities to get you moving. Set a date to complete all of your squares. Consider going over your log daily to fill in the squares, as you will not remember what activity you did three weeks from now. Make sure that your date goals are reasonable and timely.

*[[Image:Salsadancing_620.jpg|thumb|Dancing can be an aerobic workout]]For physical activity, try something different. Maybe you’ve stopped going to the gym because it's boring. Do something unique and preferably something that involves a long-term commitment and contract, such as swing or [[Dance Salsa|salsa dancing]], [[Swim|swimming lessons]], [[Learn to Fence|fencing]], or [[Choose a Martial Art|martial arts]]. Choose a school or instructor you like--you're more likely to show up, especially if there's someone holding you accountable. The more expensive the contract, the more likely you are to stick with it...unless you're filthy rich, in which case you can hire a personal trainer.

*If you are having a hard time getting started or maintaining an exercise routine, use Monday as the day to recommit. Instead of making it a New Year’s Resolution or something you start doing on your birthday, using Monday gives you fifty-two chances to get on track!

*Don't over exercise or lose too much weight. Check with your doctor if you are going to start a new and more healthy diet before you begin. Make sure you check your BMI for improvement and make sure you aren't losing too much weight (that's not good). Being underweight is also unhealthy and can increase the risk of osteoporosis.

*[[Image:Hospital 4761.jpg|thumb|Consulting the doctor.]]Consult your doctor before making any major changes to your lifestyle if you have a medical condition that could be affected.  Consulting your doctor can also help you rule out medical conditions that could be contributing to your weight.
* Don't lose weight too quickly. The harder you push yourself, the higher the chance of relapse. Slow and steady wins the race.

* Remember that being healthy overall is more important than losing weight. Preventing obesity should be like preventing diabetes or cancer or hypertension; you are preventing a disease. Never do anything unhealthful to lose weight. You don’t want to substitute one disease for another.

* Avoid "fad" diets such as the cabbage soup diet, "carb-loading," boiled egg diet, etc. Your body requires essential fats and essential amino acids (from proteins) for its bodily processes, but carbohydrates are '''not''' strictly essential because fats and proteins will be changed into glucose in ketosis through the Krebs Cycle (also called the Citric Acid Cycle)[http://porpax.bio.miami.edu/~cmallery/255/255atp/mcb6e.12.1b.jpg diagram of some Molecular Cell Biology] at the cellular mitochondrial level as part of the oxidative process of producing energy.[http://porpax.bio.miami.edu/~cmallery/255/255atp/255makeatp.htm Krebs as part of respiration, energy creation] Protein is used to build muscles, repair cells, and make hormones, such as thyroxine from tyrosine or serotonin from tryptophan. Fat is used in cellular membranes and enables the body to absorb fat-soluble vitamins, including vitamins A and D. Good fats such as olive oil or the fat in nuts may reduce the risk of heart disease by benefiting lipid profiles and unclogging arteries.

Carbohydrates are ''used'' for one purpose: energy--burning carbohydrates for energy. Some excess carbohydrates are turned into glycogen and stored in the liver, then if there is more than the liver can retain, then it is converted to body fat. Carbohydrates raise blood sugar and stimulate the production of insulin, a hormone that transports glucose to fat cells for storage; fats and proteins can be used for energy without a raise in blood sugar. Nutritionists have the glycemic index to measure how quickly foods increase blood sugar. Foods without carbs do '''not''' raise blood sugar and aren’t even assigned GI values. “There are no GI values given for meat, poultry, fish, avocados, salad vegetables, cheese, or eggs because these foods contain little or no carbohydrate and it would be exceedingly difficult for people to consume a portion of the foods containing 50 g or even 25 g of available carbohydrate. Even in large amounts, these foods when eaten alone are not likely to induce a significant rise in blood glucose.”[http://www.ajcn.org/cgi/content/full/76/1/5 '''Kaye Foster-Powell, Susanna H. A. Holt, and Janette C. Brand-Miller.''' July 2002. International Table of Glycemic Index and Glycemic Load Values: 2002. American Journal of Clinical Nutrition 76(1):5-56]

Carbohydrates are '''not''' necessary for life; when in ketosis, the body produces glucose from protein. This is healthy in the long-term and the most effective way to lose weight, provided you make it a lifetime commitment. Constantly switching from carbs to no carbs and back is more dangerous than just eating the carbs and staying fat.
*Don't look up to celebrities for their diets.The chemical diets ''will not'' work. All of us want to keep fit, but most of all healthy.

# [[Image:Bowlmaccheese_73.jpg|thumb|Big bowl, big servings, big weight gain]]'''Downsize your kitchenware.''' The human mind works in mysterious ways. It turns out that using smaller bowls, plates, and containers can subconsciously influence how much you serve yourself. Even nutrition experts are victims of this phenomenon; when 85 of them were given a random mix of small and large bowls and scoops, those who got larger bowls served themselves 31% more ice cream, and added on another 14.5% if they had bigger scoops!<ref>[http://cat.inist.fr/?aModele=afficheN&cpsidt=18069027 '''Brian Wansink, Koert van Ittersum, and James E. Painter.''' September 2006. Ice Cream Illusions: Bowls, Spoons, and Self-Served Portion Sizes. American Journal of Preventive Medicine. 31(3):240-243]</ref>

# [[Image:Utensils_643.jpg|thumb]]'''Put down the knife.''' By putting down whatever utensils you're using between every bite, you can significantly slow down your eating time, leaving your stomach a chance to feel full and reducing the likelihood that you'll go for seconds. Another technique that can have a similar effect is to [[Drink More Water Every Day|take a sip]] between each bite. Numerous studies have shown that eating slowly results in eating less.<ref>[http://www.livescience.com/health/061115_eating_slow.html Science Confirms Diet Tactic: Eat Slow, Eat Less]</ref> There's even a device you can get from a dentist that you wear to make your oral cavity smaller so that you take smaller bites,<ref name="webmd" /> and a fork that's so awkward to use that you'll get less food per bite!<ref>[http://www.dietfork.com The Diet Fork]</ref>

#[[Image:Wholegrainpasta_466.jpg|thumb|Whole grain pasta]]'''Choose whole grains over a whole belly.''' If you switch out all of your refined grain food (white bread, food made with white flour) for whole-grain food (oatmeal, whole-grain cereal, whole-grain pasta, brown rice and barley) you won't lose additional weight overall. # '''Focus on the tried and true.''' Ultimately, losing weight comes down to one key principle: Burn more calories than you consume. The steps that follow won't work if you have a thousand more calories coming into your body on a daily basis than you have going out. Lay the foundation for weight loss with these practices:
#*Count calories and [[Keep a Food Diary|keep a food diary]].
#*[[Keep to Your Diet|Go on a diet.]]
#*Cut down on [[Eat Less Sugar|sugar]], [[Avoid High Fructose Corn Syrup|high fructose corn syrup]], [[Avoid Trans Fats|trans fats]] and [[Limit Your Saturated Fat Intake|saturated fats]].
#* Burn more calories by [[Exercise|exercising]]: [[Run]], [[Walk|walk]], even [[Exercise While Sitting at Your Computer|exercise at the computer]] you are sitting in front of now.
#* [[Increase Your Metabolism|Raise your metabolism.]]

# [[Image:Bowlmaccheese_73.jpg|thumb|Big bowl, big servings, big weight gain]]'''Downsize your kitchenware.''' The human mind works in mysterious ways. It turns out that using smaller bowls, plates, and containers can subconsciously influence how much you serve yourself. Even nutrition experts are victims of this phenomenon; when 85 of them were given a random mix of small and large bowls and scoops, those who got larger bowls served themselves 31% more ice cream, and added on another 14.5% if they had bigger scoops!<ref>[http://cat.inist.fr/?aModele=afficheN&cpsidt=18069027 '''Brian Wansink, Koert van Ittersum, and James E. Painter.''' September 2006. Ice Cream Illusions: Bowls, Spoons, and Self-Served Portion Sizes. American Journal of Preventive Medicine. 31(3):240-243]</ref>

# [[Image:Utensils_643.jpg|thumb]]'''Put down the knife.''' By putting down whatever utensils you're using between every bite, you can significantly slow down your eating time, leaving your stomach a chance to feel full and reducing the likelihood that you'll go for seconds. Another technique that can have a similar effect is to [[Drink More Water Every Day|take a sip]] between each bite. Numerous studies have shown that eating slowly results in eating less.<ref>[http://www.livescience.com/health/061115_eating_slow.html Science Confirms Diet Tactic: Eat Slow, Eat Less]</ref> There's even a device you can get from a dentist that you wear to make your oral cavity smaller so that you take smaller bites,<ref name="webmd" /> and a fork that's so awkward to use that you'll get less food per bite!<ref>[http://www.dietfork.com The Diet Fork]</ref>

# [[Image:Oatmealcookies_579.jpg|thumb]]'''Know thy enemy.''' Make a list of the food items that are your weaknesses. These aren't always unhealthy foods, either. Sometimes we fool ourselves into believing that as long as we avoid the "bad" foods, we're making progress. At least, that's what we like to think as we get up for our third serving of fruit salad, or finish a bag of pretzels in one sitting, saying that they're healthier than chips. Remember that too much of anything is bad. You probably don't need to keep a [[Keep a Food Diary|food diary]] to know your enemies. Common culprits include [[Quit Soda Pop|soda]], bread, [[Quit Drinking Alcohol|alcohol]], and [[Overcome an Addiction to Fast Food|fast food]]. Whatever your weakness is, cut down on it. If you cut it out completely, you're more likely to binge. Buy only small packages of it and have it only once in a while. If cutting down doesn't work, you might need to go cold turkey.

#[[Image:Wholegrainpasta_466.jpg|thumb|Whole grain pasta]]'''Choose whole grains over a whole belly.''' If you switch out all of your refined grain food (white bread, food made with white flour) for whole-grain food (oatmeal, whole-grain cereal, whole-grain pasta, brown rice and barley) you won't lose additional weight overall. However, you ''will'' lose more weight in the belly area, which will make you look thinner--at least, that's what a Penn State study implies.<ref name="drweil">http://www.drweil.com/drw/u/QAA400379/Whole-Grains-Shrink-Belly-Fat.html</ref> Not only will your slimmer profile make you feel better about your progress, but by losing the VAT (visceral adipose tissue) you're also doing away with a risk factor for [[Prevent Type 2 Diabetes|type 2 diabetes]], coronary vascular disease, and some types of [[Celebrate Cancer Awareness Month|cancer]].<ref>[http://www.wwltv.com/local/stories/wwl043008mlfarris.b6d54301.html Whole Grains Shrinks Belly Fat]</ref> Check those labels and make sure that any grain-based foods you buy are made up of at least fifty-one percent whole grain.<ref name="drweil" />

# [[Image:Grocerylist_537.jpg|thumb]]'''Limit your spending.''' Some people have an easier time [[Save Money|controlling their wallet]] than controlling their diet. Go ahead, cut up those credit cards, and build up your emergency fund, if you haven't already (in its own account, and leave the bank card at home). Limit the amount of cash you have in your wallet, especially if you're subject to spontaneous fast food indulgences. When you go grocery shopping, have a list prepared, and bring just enough money to cover those items (this might take a few dry runs). The embarrassment of not having enough money at the register will keep you from throwing a few extra items in the shopping cart. If you don't do the grocery shopping, then offer to take on this monumental role. Your family or roommates might complain about the absence of junk food, but you'll be doing them a favor by stocking the kitchen with healthy stuff. They'll thank you...later...years later.

# [[Image:Digitalwatch_476.jpg|thumb]]'''Set a digital watch to go off every two hours.''' Eat only when the watch tells you to. Spontaneous eating sessions (those times when you feel those hunger pangs, those [[Stop Sweet Cravings|cravings]], and you scour the cabinets or the streets in search of satisfaction) are your weakest points. This is why all weight loss books tell you to avoid skipping meals. If you eat every two hours, you won't get so hungry that you gorge yourself when you do eat. You know how it goes: "Oh...I'm so hungry...the brownies are right there...I'd have to walk all the way to the deli to get a sandwich, but my stomach's churning...." Of course, if you eat the equivalent of a cheeseburger every two hours, that's a recipe for obesity, but again, you're more likely to retain self-control and stick to your diet when you don't have hunger pangs to cloud your judgment. It wouldn't hurt, however, to [[Plan Everyday Meals for Your Family|plan out what you'll eat]] (smoothie at 10, chicken salad at 12, a single piece of leftover cherry pie at 2, a slice of bread with peanut butter at 4, and so on).

#*This has the added benefit of [[Increase Your Metabolism|increasing your metabolism]]. Extending the time between meals makes your body go into "starvation mode," which will slow down your metabolism in response to the perceived threat of starvation. This is why fasting and skipping meals will only make things worse. In addition to having four to six small meals per day,<ref>[http://www.webmd.com/diet/features/rev-up-your-metabolism Rev Up Your Metabolism]</ref> eating healthy snacks will also increase your metabolism.<ref>[http://www.webmd.com/fitness-exercise/guide/make-most-your-metabolism Make the Most of Your Metabolism]</ref>

#*Another useful way to think about this is to use a "hunger scale." Rate your hunger on a scale of 0 to 10, with 0 being so hungry that you feel weak and 10 being so full that you just want to curl up in bed and digest. Eat when you're at about 3, which is when you're just a little hungry, but not famished.<ref>[http://www.thedietchannel.com/kick-new-year-with-10-tips Kick the New Year Right With These 10 Diet Tips]</ref>

# [[Image:Cash_975.jpg|thumb]]'''Trade weight for cash.''' A 2007 study showed that the more you pay people to lose weight, the more pounds they drop over a three-month period.<ref>[http://www.joem.org/pt/re/joem/abstract.00043764-200709000-00008.htm;jsessionid=L0GVF1XFGN33yJ8x69T4TLlr6PJ9bkJn2yJF56yvCGQRPNth4CQh!-573288796!181195629!8091!-1 '''Eric A. Finkelstein, Laura A. Linnan, Deborah F. Tate, Ben E. Birken.''' September 2007. A Pilot Study Testing the Effect of Different Levels of Financial Incentives on Weight Loss among Overweight Employees. Journal of Occupational & Environmental Medicine. 49(9):981-989.]</ref> If there's someone who keeps nagging you to lose weight, ask that person about paying you for every pound you lose. If your employer is self-insured, he or she might consider enlisting the services of a company that develops reward programs to encourage employees to lose weight.<ref>[http://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2007/11/10/AR2007111000074_pf.html An Economy of Scales: Paying People to Lose Weight Helps Drop Pounds and Health-Care Costs]</ref> You can also sign a contract that forces you to pay up for every pound you don't lose (or every pound you gain)<ref>[https://stickk.com StickK]</ref> and whatever money you pay (or gain) can be [[Give Charity Donations Safely|donated to charity]].

# '''Exercise and Save $$$ at the same time''' Walk to the store or library. Whenever your destination is close enough (half a mile one way is enough, especially if you are going to push or carry groceries) Drive only if you are planning to go more than a mile one way or when the weather isn't good.

* You don't have to put on sweats and sneakers or hit the gym to lose weight. You can do some garden work and vacuum the floor on your own property. Picking up toys is good exercise, too.

* Keep a fitness log: Get a blank piece of paper and draw about forty small squares or print a spreadsheet from Microsoft Excel a spreadsheet. Try to figure out your most common exercise-related activities and make two letter (or number) codes for them. Add a few more activities to get you moving. Set a date to complete all of your squares. Consider going over your log daily to fill in the squares, as you will not remember what activity you did three weeks from now. Make sure that your date goals are reasonable and timely.

*[[Image:Salsadancing_620.jpg|thumb|Dancing can be an aerobic workout]]For physical activity, try something different. Maybe you’ve stopped going to the gym because it's boring. Do something unique and preferably something that involves a long-term commitment and contract, such as swing or [[Dance Salsa|salsa dancing]], [[Swim|swimming lessons]], [[Learn to Fence|fencing]], or [[Choose a Martial Art|martial arts]]. Choose a school or instructor you like--you're more likely to show up, especially if there's someone holding you accountable. The more expensive the contract, the more likely you are to stick with it...unless you're filthy rich, in which case you can hire a personal trainer.

*If you are having a hard time getting started or maintaining an exercise routine, use Monday as the day to recommit. Instead of making it a New Year’s Resolution or something you start doing on your birthday, using Monday gives you fifty-two chances to get on track!
*To lose weight<ref>[http://www.101diettips.com/ Lose Weight from 101diettips.com]</ref> consistently, take the stairs instead of escalators and elevators and take brisk walks everyday.
*Follow a simple program that includes a easy to follow meal plan, exercise plan and supplement plan.

added: # [[Image:Utensils_643.jpg|thumb]]'''Put down the knife.''' By putting down whatever utensils you're using between every bite, you can significantly slow down your eating time, leaving your stomach a chance to feel full and reducing the likelihood that you'll go for seconds. Another technique that can have a similar effect is to [[Drink More Water Every Day|take a sip]] between each bite. Numerous studies have shown that eating slowly results in eating less.<ref>[http://www.livescience.com/health/061115_eating_slow.html Science Confirms Diet Tactic: Eat Slow, Eat Less]</ref> There's even a device you can get from a dentist that you wear to make your oral cavity smaller so that you take smaller bites,<ref name="webmd" /> and a fork that's so awkward to use that you'll get less food per bite!<ref>[http://www.dietfork.com The Diet Fork]</ref>

* Avoid "fad" diets such as the cabbage soup diet, "carb-loading," boiled egg diet, etc. Your body requires essential fats and essential amino acids (from proteins) for its bodily processes, but carbohydrates are '''not''' strictly essential because fats and proteins will be changed into glucose in ketosis through the Krebs Cycle (also called the Citric Acid Cycle)[http://porpax.bio.miami.edu/~cmallery/255/255atp/mcb6e.12.1b.jpg diagram of some Molecular Cell Biology] at the cellular mitochondrial level as part of the oxidative process of producing energy.[http://porpax.bio.miami.edu/~cmallery/255/255atp/255makeatp.htm Krebs as part of respiration, energy creation] Protein is used to build muscles, repair cells, and make hormones, such as thyroxine from tyrosine or serotonin from tryptophan. Fat is used in cellular membranes and enables the body to absorb fat-soluble vitamins, including vitamins A and D. Good fats such as olive oil or the fat in nuts may reduce the risk of heart disease by benefiting lipid profiles and unclogging arteries.

Carbohydrates are ''used'' for one purpose: energy--burning carbohydrates for energy. Some excess carbohydrates are turned into glycogen and stored in the liver, then if there is more than the liver can retain, then it is converted to body fat. Carbohydrates raise blood sugar and stimulate the production of insulin, a hormone that transports glucose to fat cells for storage; fats and proteins can be used for energy without a raise in blood sugar. Nutritionists have the glycemic index to measure how quickly foods increase blood sugar. Foods without carbs do '''not''' raise blood sugar and aren’t even assigned GI values. “There are no GI values given for meat, poultry, fish, avocados, salad vegetables, cheese, or eggs because these foods contain little or no carbohydrate and it would be exceedingly difficult for people to consume a portion of the foods containing 50 g or even 25 g of available carbohydrate. Even in large amounts, these foods when eaten alone are not likely to induce a significant rise in blood glucose.”[http://www.ajcn.org/cgi/content/full/76/1/5 '''Kaye Foster-Powell, Susanna H. A. Holt, and Janette C. Brand-Miller.''' July 2002. International Table of Glycemic Index and Glycemic Load Values: 2002. American Journal of Clinical Nutrition 76(1):5-56]

Carbohydrates are '''not''' necessary for life; when in ketosis, the body produces glucose from protein. This is healthy in the long-term and the most effective way to lose weight, provided you make it a lifetime commitment. Constantly switching from carbs to no carbs and back is more dangerous than just eating the carbs and staying fat.
